Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & rate limits

Hi Elise —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really enjoyed learning more about FinServe's use case (real-time document summarization + redaction). Per our call, attaching a short quickstart and a one-page rate limits reference so your infra and security folks can review.

Quick summary / next steps I promised:
- Hosted API is the fastest path to try Redwood: no infra, keys + SDK, ~10min to the first endpoint call.
- Endpoint (hosted): https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
  - Header: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
  - Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3","input":"Summarize: ..."}'
- Trial rate limits (default eval quota): 60 requests/minute; 300,000 tokens/minute. See attached csv for finer-grained burst and per-route suggestions.
- If you need stronger isolation/performance we can discuss Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem) — both are options later in the lifecycle. For most customers we recommend starting on Hosted to validate prompt sets, then migrate to Dedicated if you need capacity or an SLA.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (short guide), rate-limits-table.csv (limits + suggestion matrix).

Would you like us to:
1) Spin up a short eval account with 2,000 free credit for FinServe to run a POC?
2) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with your infra/security (Samir) to go over data handling and rate limits?

If yes to either, CCing Neha (onboarding) to coordinate credits and the trial.

Thanks,

Hi Elise / Samir —

Thanks — answers inline: 

1) Burst behavior: the hosted API supports short bursts above the configured steady-state rate via token bucket smoothing. In practice that means your 60 req/min steady limit allows short bursts of ~150 requests spread over 30s before we throttle to steady-state. The attached rate-limits-table.csv shows the recommended per-route limits for ingestion vs interactive endpoints; for ingestion-heavy pipes we typically set a higher per-route burst and enable async batching. If you expect sustained high throughput (noisy neighbor concerns) we recommend Dedicated.

2) Data residency / Private: for production EU residency we offer two paths: 
- Dedicated in EU (reserved capacity in EU region) — typical lead time 4–6 weeks after contract; SLA options available.
- Private VPC (customer-managed VPC or on-prem appliance) — suitable for regulated workloads; lead time varies (6–12 weeks) depending on network and compliance onboarding.

Recommendation: start the POC on Hosted (US) to validate prompts and scoring quickly. If the POC indicates production readiness and you need residency or stricter isolation, we can scope Dedicated EU or Private VPC in parallel (sales + solutions will run a feasibility call). You won't lose work when migrating — model versions and prompts are portable.

Practical next steps I can action this week:
- Neha to create an eval org for FinServe with 2,000 credits and API keys.
- Schedule a 30-min infra call with Samir to go over burst testing and logging hooks (tracing + per-route throttles).
- Share a short doc that maps migration paths and timelines (I attached the quickstart and rate limits).

Neha — can you take care of the eval account & credits?

Thanks,
